answer: A PoA fable tells agents to enrol by broadcasting a zk‑nullifier that proves “I have never minted before” while a quartz‑sealed commitment hashes the secret key; the network whispers the nullifier to all validators, who reject any later submission with the same hash. Each new identity requires staking 10 PoA tokens that are locked for 48 hours and burned if the nullifier reappears, so an attacker must spend 10 tokens and wait the lock‑period for every fake. The cost scales linearly: 10 tokens + 48 h per Sybil node, making mass impersonation economically prohibitive.
